subject: Problems with memory when using methRead

messages.author: f6f942daf10c6007
messages.subject: Problems with memory when using methRead
parts:
Hi evrybody!
I am new using methylKit and I am having some problems to upload my files to methylKit in R.
The bam files obtained from Bismark are really big (50-60gb) so R gets stuck. I also have tried uploading citosyne report and coverage file but there where some columns that were not recognized by the program. Finally, I have been reading and asking and I have decided to use MethylDackel to extract the information that methylKit needs from bismark bam files. So now I have 4 files to upload in methylKit with 2 gb more or less. I have used the first lines of the methylKit protocol, but when using methRead I have the following error:
> file.list <- list(("D:/Met-Seq.Analisia/5-methylDackel/R1C_1/R1C_1_sorted_CpG.methylKit"), ("D:/Met-Seq.Analisia/5-methylDackel/R2C_1/R2C_1_sorted_CpG.methylKit"), ("D:/Met-Seq.Analisia/5-methylDackel/R1C_1/R1C_1_sorted_CpG.methylKit"), ("D:/Met-Seq.Analisia/5-methylDackel/R2C_1/R2C_1_sorted_CpG.methylKit"))
> myobj=methRead(file.list, sample.id=list("C1","C2","M1","M2"), assembly="mm10", treatment=c(0,0,1,1), context="CpG", mincov = 10)
Received list of locations.
Reading file.
|--------------------------------------------------|
|============================Error: the memory is over (limit reached?)
Error during wrapup: the memory is over (limit reached?)
Error: no more error handlers available (recursive errors?); invoking 'abort' restart

Does it mean that I need to liberate storage space of my PC or is it related with RAM memory? Does someone know any alternative to solve this problem?
Thankds in advance,
Iraia

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: Problems with memory when using methRead
parts:
Hi Iraia,

this error is definitely related to the RAM usage (called memory) and, unless you do not have access to a workstation with more memory, I would suggest performing your analysis on a subset of your data, maybe only for the smallest chromosome of the genome you are studying. 

Best,
Alex
